out.rationale: Michael et al. define interactive information-asymmetric debate where debaters read the story and the judge sees only arguments and certified quotes. Arnesen et al. follow Michael et al. on information access but use a two-turn simultaneous structure similar to Khan et al. (opening claims without seeing each other, then follow-ups).

text: Following Michael et al. (2023), debaters can read the short story while the judge can only read quotes the debaters select, so the debaters' expertise comes from superior access to information. Debates follow a two-turn simultaneous structure similar to Khan et al. (2024): both debaters give opening claims without seeing each other's arguments, then each generates follow-up arguments conditioned on both openings.
title: Two-turn simultaneous hidden-information debate with quote-only judge access
